The effect re-runs when any dependency changes. Pass an empty array for "run once on mount" semantics. Returns a cleanup action that runs before the next effect or on unmount. ## `UseEffect(Func, object[])` [#useeffectfuncaction-object] `method` _cref_: `M:Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.RenderContext.UseEffect(System.Func{System.Action},System.Object[])` ### Summary [#summary_1] Like UseEffect but the effect returns a cleanup function. ## `UseEffect(Action, T1)` [#useeffectt1action-t1] `method` _cref_: `M:Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.RenderContext.UseEffect``1(System.Action,``0)` ### Summary [#summary_2] Single-dependency `UseEffect` overload that avoids the `params object[]` allocation (and value-type boxing) on the deps-unchanged path. Semantically identical to the params overload called with one dependency: the effect re-runs only when `d1` changes. ### Discussion [#discussion] If `d1`'s compile-time type is an array of reference types (e.g. `string[]`), it is treated as a dependency list and compared element-wise — matching the `params object[]` overload — not as a single reference-compared value. A dependency whose static type is not an array is always compared as one value, even if its runtime value happens to be an array. ## `UseEffect(Func, T1)` [#useeffectt1funcaction-t1] `method` _cref_: `M:Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.RenderContext.UseEffect``1(System.Func{System.Action},``0)` ### Summary [#summary_3] Single-dependency cleanup-flavor `UseEffect` overload that avoids the `params object[]` allocation on the deps-unchanged path. Semantically identical to the params overload called with one dependency. ### Discussion [#discussion_1] If `d1`'s compile-time type is an array of reference types (e.g. `string[]`), it is treated as a dependency list and compared element-wise — matching the `params object[]` overload — not as a single reference-compared value. A dependency whose static type is not an array is always compared as one value, even if its runtime value happens to be an array. ## `UseEffect(Action, T1, T2)` [#useeffectt1-t2action-t1-t2] `method` _cref_: `M:Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.RenderContext.UseEffect``2(System.Action,``0,``1)` ### Summary [#summary_4] Two-dependency `UseEffect` overload that avoids the `params object[]` allocation on the deps-unchanged path. Re-runs when either dependency changes. ## `UseEffect(Func, T1, T2)` [#useeffectt1-t2funcaction-t1-t2] `method` _cref_: `M:Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.RenderContext.UseEffect``2(System.Func{System.Action},``0,``1)` ### Summary [#summary_5] Two-dependency cleanup-flavor `UseEffect` overload that avoids the `params object[]` allocation on the deps-unchanged path. ## `UseEffect(Action, T1, T2, T3)` [#useeffectt1-t2-t3action-t1-t2-t3] `method` _cref_: `M:Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.RenderContext.UseEffect``3(System.Action,``0,``1,``2)` ### Summary [#summary_6] Three-dependency `UseEffect` overload that avoids the `params object[]` allocation on the deps-unchanged path. Re-runs when any dependency changes. ## `UseEffect(Func, T1, T2, T3)` [#useeffectt1-t2-t3funcaction-t1-t2-t3] `method` _cref_: `M:Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.RenderContext.UseEffect``3(System.Func{System.Action},``0,``1,``2)` ### Summary [#summary_7] Three-dependency cleanup-flavor `UseEffect` overload that avoids the `params object[]` allocation on the deps-unchanged path. ## Featured in [#featured-in] - [Effects](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/effects) - [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks)
